title: Jared Cannonier vs. Michael Page prediction, pick, start time for UFC 319
text: Jared Cannonier vs. Michael Page prediction, pick, start time for UFC 319 Jared Cannonier and Michael Page meet on the main card of UFC 319 at United Center in Chicago. Check out this quick breakdown of the matchup from MMA Junkie analyst Dan Tom. Last event: 4-2 UFC main cards, 2025: 80-60-1 Jared Cannonier vs. Michael Page UFC 319 preview Cannonier (18-8 MMA, 11-8 UFC) returned to the win column in his last outing with a fourth-round main event finish of Gregory Rodrigues in February. The result halted a two-fight skid against Nassourdine Imavov and Caio Borralho. Before those setbacks, the former title challenger won back-to-back decisions against Sean Strickland and Marvin Vettori. ... Page (23-3 MMA, 2-1 UFC) picked up his second UFC win in February, earning a unanimous decision nod against Shara Magomedov. A decision loss to Ian Machado Garry followed his debut decision win over Kevin Holland. Jared Cannonier vs. Michael Page UFC 319 expert pick, prediction Serving as a strange offering at middleweight is a matchup between Jared Cannonier and Michael Page. I'm not sure if Page even wants to fight at 185 pounds again or if this is just another case of the UFC desperately needing to fill their event schedule by any means necessary, but this fight could leave a lot of us feeling silly for ignoring Cannonier's size and on-paper grappling edge in this spot. And though I'm tempted to take a flier on the 41-year-old underdog after seeing him attend the pre-fight pressers looking like Omar from "The Wire," I can't ignore the fact that counter fighters with jabs and footwork have traditionally proven to be stylistic kryptonite for Cannonier. There is a shocking finishing upside for fighters here, but I'll officially pick Page to peck away at Cannonier from range in a fight that could be frustrating to watch. title: Cannonier Vs. Page Odds, Full Fight Preview & Prediction
text: Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) Middleweight sluggers Jared Cannonier vs. Michael Page will throw down this weekend (Sat., Aug. 16, 2025) at UFC 319 inside United Center in Chicago, Illinois. After a couple tough losses in 2024 to elite opposition, former title challenger Cannonier rebounded with one of the more entertaining Apex main events of the year, smashing “Robocop” in round three to complete a dramatic comeback (re-live that here). At 41 years old, it’s not clear how much time Cannonier has left as a high-level UFC fighter, but he remains a threat as of this moment. Page, meanwhile, joined UFC late in his career, but “Venom” is having fun with it. After coming up short to Ian Garry slowed his title dreams, Page opted to jump weight classes, taking on any interesting striker UFC is willing to throw his direction. Has the career Welterweight bitten off more than he can chew here with a former Heavyweight knockout artist? Let’s take a closer look at the betting odds and strategic keys for each athlete: Cannonier vs. Page Betting Odds - Jared Cannonier victory: +160 - Jared Cannonier via TKO/KO/DQ: +650 - Jared Cannonier via submission: +2500 - Jared Cannonier via decision: +275 - Michael Page victory: -192 - Michael Page via TKO/KO/DQ: +350 - Michael Page via submission: +2800 - Michael Page via decision: +100 - Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook How Cannonier Wins Cannonier is a formidable knockout artist with interesting wrinkles to his stand up attack. He likes to work with shifting combinations, as well as varying up the speed with which he throws his shots. In addition, he has some very nasty low kicks and an underrated dirty boxing game. Cannonier is going to face the same challenges as all Page opponents here. “MVP” is a bit taller and longer, and his whole game is built to capitalize on those physical attributes and his general ability to close distance quickly. If Cannonier tries to strike like this is a normal opponent, he’s going to be a step behind the Karate master. Cannonier has to be smart here. Those low kicks could be a great weapon, but Page is pretty accustomed to people trying to kick his legs. I’d rather see Cannonier focus on his clinch work and close distance fighter. He’s not a good enough wrestler to consistently drag Page down to the canvas, but he’s the bigger and stronger man. If he shoots merely to clinch, he could then rough Page up and break with combinations. It’s not easy to get to Page, so Cannonier has to slow him down and make those exchanges count. How Page Wins Page is a master of his craft. His long, side-on stance allows him to leap forward and backward, as well as explode into sudden kicks and jump knees. He forces everyone to play his game of long distance kickboxing, and very few are equipped in MMA to deal with his approach. His wrestling and jiu-jitsu are pretty mediocre, but that won’t matter here. The really key for Page is earning Cannonier’s respect. “Killa Gorilla” is a heavy hitter who’s been in there with the best Middleweights on the planet many times over. If he doesn’t think the Welterweight can hurt him, he’s going to swarm Page and refuse to allow him any breathing room — not optimal. Early on, Page has to find his right hand. There might be risk in committing before he feels confident, but it’s necessary. If he can crack Cannonier with a solid shot early and prove that he can hurt the bigger man, Cannonier suddenly has to respect his feints and will find himself playing Page’s game. Cannonier vs. Page Prediction There are realistic paths to victory for both men, but I am not going to pick a striker against Michael Page until he starts to lose some of his speed. The argument for Cannonier seems to be that he’ll wrestle to victory, but good takedown defense doesn’t equate to strong wrestling offense. Page knows how to shuck off and avoid the wrestling of non-elite takedown artists, and I would put Cannonier in that category. Furthermore, Page is a fast Welterweight. Opposite a 41-year-old Middleweight — even a great, seemingly ageless one — I’m expect that quickness gap to be massive and nearly impossible to overcome. Prediction: Page via decision MIDDLEWEIGHT TITLE CAR CRASH! title: UFC 319: Jared Cannonier vs. Michael Page: Live round-by-round updates
text: Jared Cannonier has long been one of the middleweights’ most durable and battle-tested fighters. A former title challenger, Cannonier's blend of knockout power and toughness makes him a dangerous opponent for anyone. His recent win over Gregory Rodrigues reminded fans that he can rally under pressure and still find the finish. Michael 'Venom' Page brings his unique brand of movement and creativity to another high-profile matchup. After years of dominating the Bellator circuit, he’s proven his style can translate to the UFC with wins over Kevin Holland and Shara Magomedov. At 38, Page still has the speed and unpredictability to frustrate traditional strikers. Cannonier’s key will be cutting off the cage and forcing exchanges, while Page will aim to maintain range and catch the veteran with counter shots. After defeating Kevin Holland and outstriking Ian Garry before dropping a narrow decision, Page moved up to middleweight and impressed with a win over hyped prospect Shara Magomedov. A victory over Jared Cannonier could position him as a dark-horse contender in an already stacked division. Unless Page abandons his game plan and engages in the kind of brawl Cannonier thrives in, this is his fight to lose. Cannonier’s size and power will keep things tense, but over three rounds, Page’s precision, speed, and tactical discipline should carry the day. Cannonier’s size might be an issue as he is naturally the bigger man, but he’s older and slower, and these types of opponents who won’t rush into a firefight are the kind that have soundly beaten him in the past. Page will be too crafty and slick for Cannonier, whose durability and looming danger of a brutal knockout shot will keep Page honest for the duration of the fight. title: Jared Cannonier vs. Michael Page: A Middleweight Showdown in the Making?
text: Jared Cannonier vs. Michael Page: A Middleweight Showdown in the Making? Jared Cannonier vs. Michael Page: A Middleweight Showdown in the Making? The UFC's middleweight division is constantly evolving, and the potential matchup between Jared "The Killa Gorilla" Cannonier and Michael "Venom" Page (MVP) has sparked significant interest among fans and analysts. This article delves into the complexities of this potential clash, examining each fighter's strengths, weaknesses, stylistic matchups, and the broader implications for the 185-pound landscape. Fighter Profiles: Jared Cannonier Jared Cannonier's journey to the top of the middleweight division is a testament to resilience and adaptability. Starting his UFC career at heavyweight and later moving to light heavyweight, Cannonier found his stride at middleweight, showcasing devastating knockout power and a surprisingly well-rounded skillset. - Strengths: Cannonier's primary weapon is his immense power. He possesses fight-ending ability in both hands and feet. His striking is precise and calculated, often setting up his power shots with feints and angles. He also boasts a solid wrestling base, which he uses primarily for defense. His chin has proven durable, allowing him to weather storms and capitalize on openings. - Weaknesses: While his wrestling defense is adequate, Cannonier can be vulnerable to takedowns from high-level wrestlers, particularly those with relentless pressure. He can sometimes be a bit slow to start, allowing opponents to gain early momentum. Also, against opponents who consistently move and don't engage in prolonged exchanges, Cannonier's power can be neutralized. - Key Wins: Notable victories include wins over Derek Brunson, Anderson Silva, Kelvin Gastelum, and Sean Strickland. These wins demonstrate his ability to defeat a diverse range of opponents, from wrestlers to strikers. title: Preview: UFC 319 ‘Du Plessis vs. Chimaev’ - Page vs. Cannonier
text: Preview: UFC 319 ‘Du Plessis vs. Chimaev’ Page vs. Cannonier Middleweights Michael Page (23-3, 2-1 UFC) vs. Jared Cannonier (18-8, 11-8 UFC)BETTING ODDS: Page (-192), Cannonier (+160) Page remains at middleweight for the second straight fight—an interesting wrinkle in what's been an interesting UFC campaign. Page’s decade-plus career with Bellator was the subject of some derision at times, as the promotion often saw fit to have him add to his highlight reel rather than test him as a potential title contender. With that said, the Englishman mostly proved himself capable of succeeding at a high level when given the opportunity. Tall and long for both welterweight and middleweight, Page fights behind a karate-based kickboxing style that has been a tough puzzle for most opponents to solve, with his last two losses—to Logan Storley in a 2022 Bellator bout and Ian Garry in what’s currently his last welterweight fight—coming against opponents who consistently hunted for a takedown, no matter how messy. After the loss to Garry, Page outclassed Sharabutdin Magomedov in a battle of strikers that looked like a one-off move up to middleweight. Instead, he stays in the weight class for what looks like a winnable matchup against Cannonier. Cannonier spent a few middling years in the UFC at heavyweight and light heavyweight before landing at middleweight, where he immediately looked like a brand-new fighter. Cannonier’s approach was still fairly basic, but “The Killa Gorilla” showed a frightening level of power in running over David Branch. From there, Cannonier quickly shot up to contention as a powerhouse athlete that opponents could often outmaneuver in theory but rarely in practice, losing only to championship-level fighters in the next few years. Robert Whittaker was able to temporarily halt Cannonier’s rise in 2020, while then-champion Israel Adesanya stayed at range and neutralized him in a 2022 title defense. Cannonier continued to plug along after his unsuccessful title shot until a rough 2024 that seems to have taken him permanently out of contention. Cannonier still looked decent but got outworked by Nassourdine Imavov and Caio Borralho in some tough wars, suggesting that the division was finally catching up to him at age 40. Cannonier had another fun main event scrap against Gregory Rodrigues earlier this year, getting a much-needed win. However, this fight against Page looks like a tough assignment unless the Brit starts showing some signs of slowing down himself. Page has an impressive highlight reel, but one of his main superpowers is being completely content to play neutralizer and take the fight out of the fight, frustrating his opponents with his elusiveness until he can force them into making a mistake. It’s unclear if the second part of that equation can happen, but even if Cannonier never turns the pace up, Page should be perfectly content pecking at him for three rounds and walking away with the victory. The pick is Page via decision. title: Jared Cannonier vs. Michael Page Set for UFC 319
text: A rather interesting middleweight paring is set for UFC 319, as Michael “Venom” Page will face former title challenger Jared Cannonier at the Pay-Per-View event. Promotion officials confirmed the booking following an initial report by Magic MMA Bets that specified the match-up, but not the intended date. The pairing has now landed on the Chicago PPV card, which takes place at the United Center on August 16, 2025. Cannonier (18-8) sits ranked at #7 in the middleweight division, with the 41-year old reminding fight fans of the threat he poses by stopping Gregory “Robocop” Rodrigues back in February. That win snapped a two-fight skid; overall, Cannonier is 3-2 since losing a 2022 title shot opposite Israel Adesanya. Bellator alum Michael Page (23-3) has been hot since arriving in the UFC last year. He’s picked up wins over Kevin Holland (at welterweight) and Shara Bullet (at 185lbs, becoming the first to defeat the Dagestani star). His lone loss in the UFC so far came to Ian Machado Garry; UFC 319 will mark MVP’s second straight fight at 185lbs. Page is ranked at #15 in the 170lb division, and is not currently ranked at middleweight. UFC 319 is headlined by a middleweight title fight that sees Dricus Du Plessis looking to defend his belt against the imposing Khamzat Chimaev. title: Jared Cannonier vs. Michael Page Set for UFC 319
text: A rather interesting middleweight paring is set for UFC 319, as Michael “Venom” Page will face former title challenger Jared Cannonier at the Pay-Per-View event. Promotion officials confirmed the booking following an initial report by Magic MMA Bets that specified the match-up, but not the intended date. The pairing has now landed on the Chicago PPV card, which takes place at the United Center on August 16, 2025. Cannonier (18-8) sits ranked at #7 in the middleweight division, with the 41-year old reminding fight fans of the threat he poses by stopping Gregory “Robocop” Rodrigues back in February. That win snapped a two-fight skid; overall, Cannonier is 3-2 since losing a 2022 title shot opposite Israel Adesanya. Bellator alum Michael Page (23-3) has been hot since arriving in the UFC last year. He’s picked up wins over Kevin Holland (at welterweight) and Shara Bullet (at 185lbs, becoming the first to defeat the Dagestani star). His lone loss in the UFC so far came to Ian Machado Garry; UFC 319 will mark MVP’s second straight fight at 185lbs. Page is ranked at #15 in the 170lb division, and is not currently ranked at middleweight. UFC 319 is headlined by a middleweight title fight that sees Dricus Du Plessis looking to defend his belt against the imposing Khamzat Chimaev. title: Jared Cannonier vs. Michael Page added to UFC 319
text: Jared Cannonier vs. Michael Page added to UFC 319 A middleweight fight between Jared Cannonier and Michael "Venom" Page has been added to UFC 319, the promotion announced Friday. The card - which takes place Aug. 16 in Chicago - will be headlined by a middleweight title fight between champion Dricus Du Plessis and Khamzat Chimaev. Page is 2-1 since debuting in the UFC in March 2024. The former Bellator star moved from welterweight to middleweight to defeat Sharabutdin Magomedov in his most recent Octagon appearance in February. Meanwhile, Cannonier snapped a two-fight losing streak by defeating Gregory Rodrigues in February. The former title challenger is 11-8 in the UFC. Cannonier is the seventh-ranked middleweight in the UFC, while Page shows as the promotion's No. 15 welterweight.
